https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-assessmen.notes: Advice MAP -> eutex:hasTestStandard. The upstream property links an assessment method to the standard that defines it, which is already represented by eutex:hasTestStandard in our vocabulary.
Advice MAP -> oec:testedConditions. The upstream ‘specifies condition’ concept aligns with our existing property that describes the conditions under which a test or assessment is performed.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-associate.notes: Advice MAP -> eutex:chemicalPurpose. The upstream concept ‘has textile chemical function’ is equivalent to our existing property eutex:chemicalPurpose, which describes the purpose of a chemical in textile manufacturing.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-connector.notes: Advice MAP -> oec:SingleValuedDataElement. The upstream class ‘QuantitativeValue’ is equivalent to our existing class oec:SingleValuedDataElement, which represents a single data point with a numeric value and unit.

Advice MAP -> eucpr:hasCharacteristicValue. The upstream property ‘hasMeasurementUnit’ is functionally equivalent to our existing eucpr:hasCharacteristicValue, which already associates a quantitative value with its unitCode.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-core#Reus.notes: Advice OUT_OF_SCOPE. The class represents a product type that is explicitly excluded from the DPP scope, so it does not need to be modeled in our vocabulary.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-core#hasF.notes: Advice MAP -> oec:massFraction. The upstream property represents a mass fraction of a fibre component, which is exactly what oec:massFraction captures.
Advice MAP -> eutex:FiberType. The upstream property links a fibre composition component to its fibre type, which is exactly what eutex:FiberType represents.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-core#hasT.notes: Advice MAP -> oec:massFraction. The upstream property represents the mass fraction of textile fibres, which is exactly what oec:massFraction captures.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-core#jrcE.notes: Advice MAP -> eudr:exemptionReasonCode. The upstream property captures a coded reason for exclusion from the JRC study scope, which aligns with eudr:exemptionReasonCode’s purpose of representing an exemption reason code.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-durabilit.notes: Advice MAP -> eutex:abrasionResistance. The upstream class represents abrasion resistance, which is already captured by eutex:abrasionResistance.

Advice MAP -> eutex:VisualInspectionResult. Colour depth and evenness is a visual inspection sub‑rating that is already represented by eutex:VisualInspectionResult, which captures colour change and other visual quality metrics.

Advice MAP -> eutex:VisualInspectionResult. Colour fading is a visual failure mode that falls under the colour change sub‑rating of eutex:VisualInspectionResult, which already captures colour intensity loss during use or washing.

Advice MAP -> eutex:colorFastness. Colour fastness is directly represented by eutex:colorFastness, which captures the resistance of textile colour to fading, running or alteration under standard test conditions.
Advice MAP -> eutex:dimensionalStability. Dimensional stability is already represented by eutex:dimensionalStability, which captures the maximum dimensional change after washing.

Advice MAP -> eutex:hasDurabilityInfo. The upstream property ‘has durability aspect’ is conceptually equivalent to the existing eutex:hasDurabilityInfo, which links a textile product to its durability metrics.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#C.notes: Advice MAP -> eutex:CareInstruction. The upstream CareMethodConcept is a controlled value for textile care, which aligns with our eutex:CareInstruction class that represents ISO 3758:2023 care instructions.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#D.notes: Advice MAP -> eubat:TemperatureRange. Dyeing temperature is a specific instance of a temperature range used in an operating context, which aligns with the generic TemperatureRange concept.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#R.notes: Advice MAP -> euelec:recyclingProcess. The upstream concept is a generic recycling process, which directly corresponds to the existing euelec:recyclingProcess class.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#T.notes: Advice CARRIER -> EPCIS event. A textile process execution is a concrete occurrence that maps directly to an EPCIS event with CBV bizStep and disposition.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#U.notes: Advice CARRIER -> EPCIS event (bizStep: use or wear). The use‑or‑wear process is a lifecycle event that can be represented by an EPCIS event with the appropriate CBV bizStep.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#W.notes: Advice CARRIER -> EPCIS event (bizStep: washing). A washing process is a lifecycle event that can be captured by an EPCIS event with the appropriate CBV bizStep.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#h.notes: Advice MAP -> eutex:hasCareInstructions. The upstream property ‘has care instruction’ is equivalent to the existing eutex:hasCareInstructions, which links a textile product to its care instructions.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#i.notes: Advice CARRIER -> EPCIS event. The relationship is already expressed by the EPCIS ProductEvent that records the process execution; no new property is required.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#r.notes: Advice CARRIER -> EPCIS event. The relationship is already expressed by the EPCIS ProductEvent that records or represents a process execution; no new property is required.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#u.notes: Advice MAP -> eutex:chemicalPurpose. The upstream property ‘uses chemical function’ aligns with our existing eutex:chemicalPurpose, which captures the technical purpose of a chemical in textile processes.

Advice MAP -> eutex:hasTextileChemicals. The upstream property ‘uses chemical substance’ describes a textile process’s use of a specific chemical, which aligns with our existing eutex:hasTextileChemicals that records the chemicals used in textile production.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-recyclabi.notes: Advice MAP -> eudr:verificationMethod. The upstream class describes a verification method based on a manufacturer’s declaration, which is conceptually equivalent to the generic Verification Method used in eudr for deforestation‑free and legality claims.

Advice MAP -> eutex:RecyclabilityAssessment. The upstream class describes a textile product’s potential to provide fibre or material feedstock under specified recycling contexts, which aligns with the eutex:RecyclabilityAssessment concept that scores recyclability based on composition and technical factors.
Advice MAP -> eutex:hasSortingFactors. The upstream property ‘applies sorting criterion’ aligns with our existing eutex:hasSortingFactors, which captures the factors used in sorting for recycling.

Advice MAP -> eutex:hasRecyclabilityAssessment. The upstream property ‘assesses recyclability of’ directly corresponds to our eutex:hasRecyclabilityAssessment, which links a textile product to its recyclability assessment.

Advice MAP -> euelec:hasMaterialRecoveryResults. The upstream property links a recycling event to recovered material, which is already represented by euelec:hasMaterialRecoveryResults in our vocabulary.
Advice MAP -> eutex:hasRecyclabilityAssessment. The upstream property links a product to its recyclability aspect, which is already represented by eutex:hasRecyclabilityAssessment in our vocabulary.

Advice MAP -> eutex:hasWasteOriginType. The upstream concept ‘has waste source type’ aligns with our existing property ‘eutex:hasWasteOriginType’, which classifies the origin of recycled waste material.

Advice MAP -> euelec:recyclingProcess. The upstream property ‘uses recycling process type’ matches the existing euelec:recyclingProcess, which relates a recycling route (or item) to its principal recycling process type.

Advice MAP -> eutex:hasRecycledContentDeclaration. The upstream property ‘verifies recycled content declaration’ expresses the same relationship as eutex:hasRecycledContentDeclaration, which links an assessment result (or product) to the structured recycled‑content declaration it verifies.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-repairabi.notes: Advice MAP -> oec:RepairabilityInfo. The upstream class ‘Possibility of refurbishment’ describes the ability to prepare, clean, test, service and repair a product to restore its performance, which is effectively the same concept as oec:RepairabilityInfo that captures repair and maintenance information per ESPR Article 7.
Advice CARRIER -> EPCIS event. A textile refurbishment occurrence is an instance of a generic EPCIS event; the existing EPCIS construct already carries this concept.
Advice CARRIER -> EPCIS event. A textile remanufacturing occurrence is an instance of a generic EPCIS event; the existing EPCIS construct already carries this concept.
Advice CARRIER -> EPCIS event. A textile repair occurrence is an instance of a generic EPCIS event; the existing EPCIS construct already carries this concept.
Advice CARRIER -> EPCIS event. A textile upgrading occurrence is an instance of a generic EPCIS event; the existing EPCIS construct already carries this concept.
Advice MAP -> euelec:repairType. The upstream property describes the type of repair action performed, which is already captured by our euelec:repairType property.
Advice MAP -> oec:ActorRole. The upstream property classifies an actor by its role in textile repair, which is already represented by our generic oec:ActorRole construct.
Advice MAP -> oec:hasRepairInstructions. The upstream property relates apparel to repair guidance, which is already represented by our oec:hasRepairInstructions construct.

Advice MAP -> oec:hasSparePartsAvailability. The upstream property describes the availability condition of spare parts for a repairability assessment, which is already represented by our oec:hasSparePartsAvailability property.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-structure.notes: Advice MAP -> eucpr:hasCharacteristicValue. The upstream property ‘has characteristic value’ directly corresponds to the existing eucpr:hasCharacteristicValue, which links a characteristic occurrence to its quantitative value.
